question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[4X-3].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{3}{{x}^{4}},\,1\le x
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[4X-3]=4\text{E}[X]-3
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{3}{2{x}^{2}}|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X-3] & =4\text{E}[X]-3 \\  & =4\cdot \frac{3}{2}-3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
